Lemma
[distance functions bound length below]

Source: petersen:page-0195 ↗ def:pet-ch5-curve-length ↗ def:pet-ch3-distance-function

1. ch5:5.3.2aLet $r:U o \mathbb R$ be a smooth distance function on an open set $U\subset (M,g)$. For every $C^\infty $ curve $c:[a,b] o M$ whose image lies in $U$, \[ r(c(b))-r(c(a))\le L(c)|_a^b. \]
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch5-distance-function-length-bound \sketch The eikonal equation and Cauchy–Schwarz give $(r\circ c)'=g( abla r,\dot c)\le |\dot c|$. Therefore

\[ L(c)=\int _a^b|\dot c|\, dt\ge \int _a^b g( abla r,\dot c)\, dt =\int _a^b (r\circ c)'\, dt=r(c(b))-r(c(a)), \]

by the fundamental theorem of calculus.

□
